5,144 births in 2024 marks Wesley's best year yet, and the rank moved in lockstep — #58, also a fresh high, up 64% from where the name stood ten years before.

This name's SSA history stretches all the way back to the dataset's start in 1880, though its recent gain is entirely a 21st-century story.

Wesley Snipes and Wes Craven anchor the shortened form in film, while Star Trek creator Gene Roddenberry (born Eugene Wesley Roddenberry) gives the full name an unexpected science-fiction connection.

jayden.text:
Jayden's fall is the sharpest in this batch: 5,134 births in 2024, 60% short of its count from ten years before, at #59 nationally — a long way down from its 2010 peak, when it briefly held #4.

The name's own history is short by comparison to most in this range, first appearing only in 1977 and gaining almost all of its volume within the following three decades.

No famous bearers appear in the enrichment data at all — a name that reached the near-top of the national chart within living memory, without a single documented namesake anywhere in its rise or fall.

nova.text:
Nova's climb over the past decade, 344%, ranks among the largest in this batch, trailing only Enzo and Lainey. Both its count and rank reached fresh territory recently — 5,044 births in 2024, though its actual peak, 5,920, came two years earlier in 2022.

What's unusual here is the data history: first recorded in 1885, just five years into the dataset, meaning Nova has technically existed as a US name for well over a century despite reading as an entirely modern invention.

The enrichment data offers no famous bearers to explain any of this — the name's popularity, like Aurora's in an earlier batch, isn't traceable to any single documented figure.

lainey.text:
No name across all five batches so far has grown faster than Lainey: 901% over the past decade, taking it to 5,147 births in 2024, a fresh high on both count and rank at #38.

That figure is almost entirely a small-base effect. Total US births under this name run to just 22,674 since it first appeared in 1968 — smaller than Thiago's total from the fourth batch — and its rank only cracked the top 50 this year for the first time.

The enrichment data lists no origin and no famous bearers, leaving one of this dataset's steepest-ever growth curves without a single traceable explanation.

christopher.text:
Christopher's rank and count moved in opposite directions for over a decade: #2, the best rank, came first in 1972, while 60,019 births, the raw-count high, took until 1984 to arrive — a reversed version of the lag pattern seen in most other names, where count typically peaks before rank does.

Total US births run past two million for this name, and the 2024 count, 5,054, sits 51% below where it stood ten years earlier.

Johnny Depp (born John Christopher Depp), Chris Pratt, and Chris Pine keep the shortened form visible in contemporary film, while director Christopher Nolan carries the full name into a different corner of the same industry.

nathan.text:
2004 was Nathan's high point on both fronts at once — 14,633 births, #20 nationally. The name has been present in SSA data every year since 1880, part of a total that now stands at 584,253 births.

Twenty years on, the retreat has been substantial: 5,010 births in 2024, 44% under its count a decade prior, at #62.

Its famous-bearer list runs across acting (Nathan Fillion, Nathan Lane), theology (20th-century archbishop Nathan Söderblom), and comedy (George Burns, born Nathan Birnbaum) — four very different careers sharing one name across roughly a century of public life.

grace.text:
Grace's rank peaked in 1883, just three years into this dataset, while 12,781 births — the raw-count high — didn't show up until 2003, a 120-year gap between the two milestones — one of the widest gaps observed across every batch so far, second only to Samuel's 121-year gap from the second batch.

531,126 total births since 1880 make it one of the larger names in this range, and the 2024 count, 5,002, is down 35% from a decade earlier.

Grace Kelly and computing pioneer Grace Hopper anchor the name across mid-century film and science, while Chloë Grace Moretz carries it into the present as a middle name rather than a given one.

nolan.text:
Nolan's count and rank diverged by eight years: 5,739 births in 2015 was the raw-count high, while #57, the best rank, only arrived in 2023 — shorter than Zoe's twelve-year gap or Joshua's thirteen-year one from earlier batches, but part of the same general pattern.

The ten-year change is nearly flat, down just 6% to 4,888 births in 2024.

Video game pioneer Nolan Bushnell anchors the name in 1970s tech history, alongside younger entertainment figures Nolan Gould and Nolan North — an odd pairing of industries that don't usually share a namesake.

waylon.text:
Waylon's 4,878 births in 2024 runs 225% ahead of its count a decade earlier, just short of the name's actual peak, 4,918, set two years earlier in 2022.

The name's data history stretches back to 1911, though it stayed at low volume through most of the 1900s.

Country musician Waylon Jennings is the clear namesake here — a specific, well-known figure rather than the documentation gap seen with fellow risers Nova or Lainey elsewhere in this batch, though whether his fame from decades ago explains a 2020s surge is something the birth data alone can't confirm.

brooks.text:
Brooks posted a 215% gain over the past decade, with both its count and rank hitting fresh highs together in 2024: 4,793 births at #67.

The name has technically been in SSA data since 1880, though its enrichment list carries only two entries, both indirect — essayist E. B. White (born Elwyn Brooks White) and logician Haskell Curry (born Haskell Brooks Curry), neither of whom used Brooks as a given name.

That thin, middle-name-only namesake record, despite a data history running the full length of the dataset, mirrors Cooper's pattern from the fourth batch — a name whose recent popularity doesn't trace back to any individual actually called by it.

andrew.text:
Andrew's 57% decline over the past decade ranks second-steepest in this batch, behind Jayden's 60%. Its rank peaked at #5 in 1988, a year after the raw count's own high of 36,205 in 1987.

Its total climbs past 1.3 million births since 1880, a longer, larger history than most of the names surrounding it in this range.

Andy Warhol (born Andrew Warhola), two US presidents (Andrew Jackson, Andrew Johnson), and industrialist Andrew Carnegie span art, politics, and business across two centuries — a name whose historical weight hasn't slowed its recent fall.

beau.text:
Beau's growth, 187% over the past decade, brought both its count and rank to new highs together in 2024: 4,694 births at #69.

Its data history is shorter than most names in this range — the first recorded year is 1932, more than five decades after the dataset's 1880 start.

Beau Biden, son of the former president, is the most politically visible bearer, alongside actor Beau Bridges — a small but concentrated namesake list for a name still relatively new to significant popularity.

willow.text:
Willow's rise, 93% over the past decade, has already passed its peak by one measure: the raw count topped out in 2021 at 5,193, while the rank kept climbing for another year, reaching #37 in 2022, before both eased to 4,653 births and #41 by 2024.

This name's records begin in 1890, a decade later than most names in this dataset, though it stayed minor for most of the twentieth century before this recent run.

Willow Smith, born in 2000, is the clearest namesake — young enough that her own career and the name's later surge are roughly contemporaries rather than one obviously causing the other.

adrian.text:
Adrian's count and rank peaked together in 2008 — 7,937 births and #56 nationally — a clean simultaneous high.

Since then the decline has been steady rather than sharp: 4,617 births in 2024, down 31% from a decade prior, landing at #72.

The bearer list here is unusually international for this batch — Romanian footballer Adrian Mutu, British double agent Kim Philby (born Harold Adrian Russell Philby), German Formula One driver Adrian Sutil — a name whose public figures span at least four countries without concentrating in any one.

weston.text:
2024 brought Weston a fresh high on both measures at once: 4,660 births, #70 nationally, up 57% from a decade before — a moderate gain compared to this batch's bigger risers like Enzo or Nova.

The name has technically been recorded since 1882, though it stayed at low volume for over a century before this recent climb.

Its enrichment data lists just two bearers, footballer Weston McKennie and musician Porter Robinson (born Porter Robinson Weston) — a thin namesake record for a name whose growth has been entirely recent.

lincoln.text:
Lincoln's rank and count moved apart by three years: 8,201 births in 2017 was the raw-count high, while #40, the best rank, took until 2020 to show up.

The past decade has been nearly flat since — down just 5% to 4,567 births in 2024, one of the mildest ten-year moves in this batch alongside Nolan's 6% dip.

Polar explorer Lincoln Ellsworth and Rhode Island politician Lincoln Chafee carry the name as a given name, while the enrichment data's inclusion of Lincoln Ellsworth's exact birth year, 1880, ties one namesake directly to the very first year this dataset covers.

emilia.text:
Emilia's 4,634 births in 2024 sits 131% higher than its count from ten years back, though it trails the name's actual peak, 4,851 in 2021 — the year count and rank both set their high points together, #40 nationally.

SSA records for this name run back to 1880, a quiet background presence for most of that span before this recent surge.

Emilia Clarke's television fame, beginning in 2011, sits right at the start of the name's climb — one of the clearer possible cultural connections in this batch, though the birth data can only show the timing lines up, not that it caused the rise.

naomi.text:
Naomi's rank and count peaked almost together — the rank reached #44, its best ever, in 2023, one year before the raw count reached its own high of 4,605 in 2024, a rare case of rank arriving slightly ahead of count rather than trailing it.

24% growth over the past decade is a moderate gain, well behind this batch's steeper risers like Willow or Emilia.

Naomi Watts, Naomi Campbell, and Naomi Klein span acting, modeling, and activism across recent decades — three very different kinds of public visibility sharing one name.

madison.text:
Madison's 56% decline over the past decade ranks third-steepest in this batch, behind Jayden and Andrew. 2001 was its high point on both fronts: 22,166 births, #2 nationally — a genuine near-chart-topping run that's since fallen to 4,563 births and #46 in 2024.

Unusually for a name this large, its data history doesn't reach back to 1880 at all — the first recorded year is 1970, a full 90 years into the dataset, among the shortest histories of any major name covered so far.

Its famous-bearer list is almost entirely young performers born in the late 1990s — Madison Beer, Madison Iseman, Madison Pettis — a generational cluster with no older reference point at all.

river.text:
River sits well below most of its neighbors in this batch: #112 nationally in 2024, the lowest rank of any name here, with 3,138 births — down from a peak of 3,503 in 2021, when its rank also hit its own best, #105, the following year.

Despite that modest current standing, the ten-year growth rate, 152%, is substantial, and this name's records begin in 1971, more recent than most but earlier than Lainey's or Madison's late arrivals.

Actor River Phoenix, who died in 1993, is the only bearer in the enrichment data — a specific, well-known namesake for a name that remains this batch's smallest by current rank despite genuine recent growth.

elena.text:
Elena's 2024 count, 4,567 births, and its best-ever rank, #45, arrived together — 75% above its count from ten years before.

This name's SSA data goes back to 1880, a long, quiet history before this recent acceleration.

Its famous-bearer list is unusually political and international — Romanian dictator's wife Elena Ceaușescu, Rome's former mayor Virginia Raggi (whose middle name is Elena), and cosmonaut-adjacent Bulgarian singer Inna (born Elena Alexandra Apostoleanu) — a spread across Eastern Europe that doesn't resemble the largely American or British namesake lists common elsewhere in this batch.

enzo.text:
Enzo's 435% growth over the past decade ranks second-largest in this batch, behind only Lainey's 901%, with 4,548 births and #74 nationally both marking fresh highs in 2024.

SSA records for this name start in 1915, though its decades-active list skips the 1940s entirely — a full decade with fewer than five recorded births — before resuming and eventually climbing sharply in the 2020s.

The namesake list here leans football, much like Thiago's in the fourth batch, though Enzo's cluster centers on Enzo Ferrari's automotive legacy at one end and contemporary players like Enzo Fernández at the other, a wider span of fields than Thiago's all-footballer list.

ian.text:
Ian's rank actually peaked two years before its raw count: #65 in 2003, versus the count's own high of 6,688 births in 2005 — a short reverse lag, the opposite direction from most names in this dataset, where count typically leads rank.

By 2024 it had eased to 4,547 births, down 17% from a decade prior, at #75.

Ian Fleming, Ian McKellen, and Motörhead's Lemmy (born Ian Fraser Kilmister) span espionage fiction, film, and heavy metal — a namesake list with real range for a name whose data history, starting in 1912, is shorter than most names this established.

kai.text:
Kai's count and rank peaked together in 2022 — 5,366 births and #59 nationally — before easing to 4,276 and #76 by 2024, a 77% rise over the full decade despite that recent pullback.

The enrichment data attributes a German origin to the name, a less obvious root than the Hawaiian or East Asian associations it's often assumed to carry, and its data history starts in 1926, later than most established names but well before its recent popularity.

Physicist Kai Siegbahn and footballer Kai Havertz anchor the name in science and sport respectively, two fields with little else in common beyond sharing this one short name.

valentina.text:
2024 brought Valentina to a fresh high on both fronts at once: 4,438 births, #47 nationally, up 60% from its count ten years earlier.

The name's data history starts in 1897, seventeen years into the dataset. It sat at low volume through most of the 1900s before this recent run.

Valentina Tereshkova, the first woman in space, anchors the name in a specific and singular historical achievement — a namesake with more individual weight than most of the loosely-connected lists elsewhere in this batch.

ryan.text:
29,909 births in 1985 was Ryan's high point by raw count; #11, the rank's own best, showed up the following year. Both numbers have been sliding since — 3,892 births and #87 by 2024, a 57% drop over just the last ten years, the steepest fall in this batch.

Nearly a million US babies have carried this name since 1906, when it first entered the data — later than most Irish-origin names of comparable size.

Ryan Gosling and Ryan Reynolds, born just four years apart, cover most of the name's current public image between them.

christian.text:
Christian's biggest single year, 16,057 births, came in 2000; its best rank, #21, held six years later in 2006. From there the count fell 50% across the following decade, landing at 4,247 births in 2024, #77 nationally.

Every decade since 1880 shows up in this name's records, unusual staying power for one whose meaning ties directly to religious identity rather than a person.

Hans Christian Andersen anchors it in 19th-century Danish storytelling; Jodie Foster, born Alicia Christian Foster, carries it as a middle name into contemporary American film.

victoria.text:
12,926 births in 1993 was Victoria's peak count; #16, its best rank, arrived five years afterward in 1998. Since then: a 47% slide over the last decade, settling at 4,267 births and #48 nationally by 2024.

Over half a million US births carry this name since 1880, and its royal weight runs deep — Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom was born in 1819, more than a century before the American name's own high point.

Victoria Beckham keeps it current in fashion; Sweden's Crown Princess Victoria keeps it current in monarchy.

stella.text:
Barely anything changed for Stella over the past decade — up just 1%, to 4,264 births in 2024, one of the smallest ten-year moves covered anywhere in this dataset. 2018 was its high-water mark: 5,163 births, #38 nationally.

This name's records stretch back to 1880, quiet through most of the 20th century before its 2010s climb.

Fashion designer Stella McCartney and actor Stella Adler keep the name visible today; Australian author Miles Franklin, born Stella Maria Sarah Miles Franklin in the 1870s, gives it an older literary root few would expect.

axel.text:
4,666 was Axel's peak count, set in 2020; #71, its best rank, took three more years to arrive, in 2023. It's eased slightly since, to 4,245 births and #78 by 2024, still up 51% from a decade earlier.

SSA records for this name stretch back to 1880, mostly quiet until the current run.

Norwegian king Haakon VII, poet Erik Axel Karlfeldt, and 17th-century statesman Axel Oxenstierna root the name deep in Nordic history, alongside contemporary footballer Axel Witsel and Belgian personal physician Axel Munthe, whose memoir remained a bestseller for decades.

delilah.text:
4,240 births and #50 nationally — both fresh territory for Delilah in 2024, up 69% from ten years before.

Only one figure appears in the enrichment data: the biblical Delilah, dated to roughly 1100 BC — younger than Leah's and Hannah's biblical references elsewhere in this batch, but older than Ezekiel's 620 BC and Isaiah's 765 BC from the fourth batch.

Nothing else shows up at all — an unusually singular, ancient anchor with no modern namesake pulling in the same direction.

aaron.text:
15,311 in 1989 marks Aaron's biggest year by count; the rank caught up five years later, reaching #28 in 1994. Both have receded since — 4,225 births and #79 in 2024, 43% down from what it counted a decade back.

Six hundred thousand-plus US births trace to this name since 1880, a solid mid-tier history — not among the dataset's largest names, but no recent arrival either.

Aaron Swartz, Aaron Burr, and Nobel-winning biologist Aaron Klug share almost nothing career-wise beyond this one name spanning tech activism, early American politics, and science.

micah.text:
Micah barely moved over the past decade, up just 7% to 3,909 births in 2024 — count and rank both landing on fresh highs the same year, #86 nationally.

Its records start in 1946, sixty-six years after the dataset begins, a short history for a name with biblical roots.

Just two names show up as namesakes — footballer Micah Richards and comedian Katt Williams, born Micah Sierra Williams — a thin record for gains this gradual, and total US births for the name reach 129,443 since 1946.

maya.text:
Maya's 7% ten-year gain lands almost exactly where Micah's does, though the paths differ: Maya's count peaked back in 2006 at 5,047, while the rank kept improving until 2023, reaching #50 — seventeen years after the count's own high point.

Records for this name begin in 1940, sixty years into the dataset — later than the oldest established names, earlier than several fresh arrivals in this same batch.

Maya Angelou gives it 20th-century literary weight; Maya Rudolph and Maya Hawke keep it current in comedy and film.

charlie.text:
Charlie's rank hit its best mark absurdly early — #20 in 1881, just a year into this whole dataset — while the count itself didn't peak until 1919, at 2,891 births. That's 38 years between the two milestones.

Even with a 23% uptick over the past decade, Charlie now sits at #176 — the lowest current position of any name in this dataset, with just 2,084 births in 2024. Growth on paper doesn't always mean climbing the chart when the base is already this small.

Charlie Chaplin and jazz great Charlie Parker anchor the name's early-to-mid-century image; Charlie Puth and Charlie Hunnam carry it into the present.

august.text:
1880 — the dataset's opening year — is also when August's rank hit its best mark, #74, putting it alongside Samuel, John, Thomas, William, and Charles as names that peaked positionally right at the start. What's stranger: the count record came separately, 144 years later in 2024, at 3,876 births — the name's best year ever, and it still ranks lower today, #88, than it did in 1880.

That record count rides on 151% growth over the past decade — a big jump, though still short of this batch's very top risers, Theo and Walker.

Economist Friedrich Hayek, chemist Svante Arrhenius, and biologist Ernst Haeckel form an unusually academic cluster of 19th- and 20th-century European scholars.

theo.text:
647% — the biggest ten-year gain in this batch, though the fifth batch's Lainey still holds the overall dataset record at 901%. Theo's own peak, on both fronts at once, landed in 2023: 4,137 births, #78 nationally, easing only slightly to 4,110 and #80 by 2024.

Just 35,340 US births total trace to this name since 1880 — a small enough base that the huge percentage growth makes more sense, the same shape seen in Thiago's and Lainey's own surges.

Two footballers, both under the accented spelling Théo, are the only entries in the enrichment data: Théo Hernandez and, oddly, 19th-century painter Théo van Rysselberghe.

walker.text:
Only Theo grew faster than Walker in this batch: 285% over the past decade. 4,248 births and #78 arrived together in 2022, before easing to 4,023 and #82 by 2024.

Records for this name go back to the dataset's 1880 start, quiet through most of the 20th century before the recent surge.

George W. Bush, whose middle name is Walker, sits alongside novelist Walker Percy and photographer Walker Evans — three men who all carried it as a middle name, not a first one.

silas.text:
4,108 births made 2024 Silas's best year on record — though the rank actually hit its own peak, #81, a year earlier in 2023, an unusual case of rank leading rather than trailing.

40% growth over the past decade lands Silas well below Theo's or Walker's much bigger jumps, though still solidly positive. Total US births for this name reach 70,949 since 1880, a modest but steady historical base.

Communist journalist John Reed carried Silas as a middle name; actor Silas Weir Mitchell is the closest thing to a direct namesake here.

hannah.text:
23,087 births in 2000 was Hannah's raw-count peak; the rank had already hit its own best, #2, two years earlier in 1998 — a genuine near-#1 run. From there: a 39% fall over the past decade, down to 4,054 births and #52 in 2024.

The enrichment data's oldest reference dates to roughly 1200 BC, the biblical mother of Samuel — older than Delilah's 1100 BC reference in this same batch, though younger than Leah's 1730 BC, also in this batch, and Jacob's 1790 BC from the third batch.

Hannah Arendt lends the name real philosophical weight; actor Hannah Murray keeps it visible on screen today.

jonathan.text:
24,348 births and #15 — Jonathan's count and rank hit their marks in the exact same year, 1988. Since then 51% has come off the count, leaving 4,018 births and #83 nationally by 2024.

870,561 US babies have carried this name since 1880, a serious historical footprint for a name that's now well off its late-1980s standing.

Jonathan Swift roots it in 18th-century satire; Jon Voight and Orlando Bloom, a generation apart, keep it current on screen; and physicist David Gross carries the full given name into contemporary science.

genesis.text:
4,351 births was Genesis's count high, set in 2016; its rank had already peaked three years earlier, at #55 in 2013. The slide since has been mild — just 8% in the past ten years, landing at 3,835 births in 2024.

Records here start comparatively late, 1964, and only one namesake shows up: industrial musician Genesis P-Orridge, active from the 1970s.

A recent data start, a single unconventional namesake, and a name pulled straight from religious text rather than a person — that combination sets Genesis apart from this batch's other biblical entries, Hannah and Delilah, whose oldest references are actual figures rather than a book title.

everett.text:
#81 in 1906 was Everett's earliest rank peak; the count didn't catch up until 2021, at 4,250 births — 115 years apart, one of the widest gaps seen anywhere in this dataset, trailing only Samuel's 121 years and Grace's 120.

56% growth over the past decade brought the name to 3,947 births in 2024, at #85 nationally.

Painter John Everett Millais and Civil War general Ambrose Burnside, who carried Everett as a middle name, anchor it in 19th-century art and military history — far older than its recent popularity would suggest.

leah.text:
6,790 births in 2009 was Leah's count peak; #24, the rank's own best, followed a year later. It's fallen 29% over the past decade since, to 3,969 births and #53 in 2024.

1730 BC is the oldest date in Leah's enrichment data, the biblical Leah — older than Hannah's and Delilah's references elsewhere in this batch, and behind only Jacob's 1790 BC from the third batch as the most ancient figure attached to any name across every batch so far.

Rashida Jones and Leah Remini keep the name current in film and TV; footballer Leah Williamson extends it into sport.

leonardo.text:
4,425 births in 2019 was Leonardo's high point by count; the rank followed three years later, reaching #75 in 2022. Growth over the decade has been modest, 15%, landing at 3,951 births in 2024.

The record here has a genuine gap — first appearing in 1885, then nothing at all through the 1890s, before resuming in the 1900s and continuing steadily since.

Leonardo da Vinci and mathematician Fibonacci, born Leonardo Bonacci, give this name roots stretching back nearly 900 years; Leonardo DiCaprio carries it into contemporary Hollywood.

jordan.text:
16,137 births in 1990 was Jordan's count peak; #26, its best rank, took another seven years to show up, in 1997. Since then it's given back 52% across the following decade, landing at 3,326 births and #104 nationally in 2024, one of the steeper declines in this batch.

Over half a million US births trace to this name since 1880, real historical weight for something now sitting well outside the top 50.

Cultural critic Jordan Peterson and footballer Jordan Henderson dominate the namesake list — entirely 21st-century figures despite the name's much older data history.

lillian.text:
10,049 births in 1920 marked Lillian's high point by count — but the rank had already hit its own best, #10, twenty-two years earlier in 1898, a reverse gap similar in direction to Charlie's, if smaller. The fall since has been steep: 44% lower across the following decade, settling at 3,882 births and #54 in 2024.

Close to half a million US births carry this name since 1880, placing it among this batch's larger names by history.

Lillian Gish and Lillian Hellman anchor it in early-to-mid-20th-century film and literature; industrial engineer Lillian Moller Gilbreth adds a scientific namesake from roughly the same era.

gael.text:
3,855 births and a fresh best-ever rank, #89 — both landed for Gael in 2024, up 113% from a decade earlier.

This name's history has a real hole in it: first recorded in 1919, then absent through the 1960s and 1970s specifically, before resuming in the 1980s and climbing steadily since.

Nearly every namesake here plays professional sport under the accented spelling Gaël — Clichy, Monfils, Kakuta — a tight cluster of contemporary French footballers and one tennis player, nothing older.

sawyer.text:
#132 nationally, with 2,756 births — Sawyer trails nearly everything else in this batch by current standing. 2015 was its actual peak on both fronts: 4,271 births, #94, the same year — followed by an unusually steep 23% decline over the past decade for a name still this far down the chart.

The record here is patchy: first appearing in 1913, then gone for decades until it resumes in the 1970s, a longer gap than Gael's own mid-century absence.

No famous bearers appear anywhere in the enrichment data — both the mid-2010s rise and the fall since remain undocumented by any single cultural reference.

robert.text:
4,866,007 total US births make Robert one of this dataset's largest names by history — behind only James's and John's even bigger totals, just ahead of Michael's and William's. Its rank hit #1 in 1924; the count itself didn't peak until 1947, at 91,654 births — 23 years separating the two records.

2024's count, 3,785, sits 43% below its own count from a decade back, at #90 nationally — a steep percentage fall for a name whose historical scale rivals the very largest in this dataset.

Bob Dylan, born Robert Allen Zimmerman, and Bob Marley, born Robert Nesta Marley, keep the shortened form alive in music; Robert Louis Stevenson anchors the full name in 19th-century literature.
